                  Key   Advantages         of  Spring                                                                                                                                                           

                  Spring   offers  high   testability    because     dependencies       are  injected    rather  than                                                                                           
                  hardcoded      —  making     it  easy to  swap    real implementations        with  mocks     in tests.                                                                                       

                  It  provides  excellent    scalability    through    support    for reactive    programming,       message                                                                                    
                  queues,    and   distributed    systems.                                                                                                                                                      

                  Spring   integrates    seamlessly      with  a wide   range    of technologies      including    relational                                                                                   
                  databases,     Kafka,   Redis,    cloud   platforms,    and   AI toolkits.                                                                                                                    

                  Its modular     design     means     you  only   include   what   your   application    actually   needs.                                                                                     

                  Core    Insight    (Interview      Point)                                                                                                                                                     

                         Spring    turns  plain  POJO     methods      into powerful    enterprise     features   using                                                                                         
                         three   mechanisms:       AOP     proxies,    Annotations,       and   Configuration       over                                                                                        
                         coding.                                                                                                                                                                                

                  You  write   a plain  Java   method.     Spring    wraps   it with  the  infrastructure    it needs    —  a                                                                                   
                  transaction,    a security    check,   a  remote    endpoint,    a message      listener   —   without   you                                                                                  
                  ever  touching    those    APIs   directly.                                                                                                                                                   

                  9.  Pitfalls       &    Common             Mistakes                                                                                                                                           

                  ❌   Overusing        Annotations                                                                                                                                                              

                  Stacking   too many    annotations    (@Transactional,         @Cacheable,       @Async     on  the same                                                                                      
                  method)   hides   complex    behavior   and  makes    debugging     hard.                                                                                                                     

                  ❌   Wrong       Bean    Scope                                                                                                                                                                 

                  Using  singleton       for stateful objects   (e.g., shopping    cart) →   shared   state  across  users   →                                                                                  
                  data  corruption.                                                                                                                                                                             

                  ❌   Mixing      MVC     and   WebFlux                                                                                                                                                         

                  They  use   different request   processing    models    and  cannot   be  combined     in the same                                                                                            
                  application.

SMART CONTACT MANAGER — SYSTEM DESIGN
SYSTEM DESIGN DOCUMENT · V1
Smart Contact Manager
Architecture and design reference for the SCM application — a Spring Boot contact management system with federated authentication, media hosting, and paginated search.
01  Complete system architecture
The application follows a layered Spring Boot architecture: browser requests pass through a security filter chain, into MVC controllers, down through the service layer, and out to either the relational database or external integrations (Cloudinary, SMTP, OAuth providers).

	Tables: users, users_contact, social_link, roles

02  Layer-by-layer breakdown
Presentation — Thymeleaf & Tailwind UI
Master layout (base.html) implements Thymeleaf's hierarchical fragment pattern via th:replace="~{base :: parent(...)}", consolidating shared scripts, global Tailwind/Flowbite styles, and dynamic document titles.
Component fragments are isolated into independent templates:
1. navbar.html — site navigation, responsive menu toggles, dark-mode switching, profile badges
1. sidebar.html — authenticated links: Dashboard, Profile, Add Contact, Contact Directory
1. message.html — dynamic alert component reading ${session.message}, cleared via @sessionHelper.removeMessage()
View contracts use bi-directional form binding with th:object / th:field="*{...}", with validation errors rendered via th:errors.
Security & session isolation
AUTHORIZATION FILTERING
Public routes: /, /home, /about, /services, /contact, /register, /authenticate, /do-register
Protected routes: /user/** strictly locked behind the ROLE_USER authority.
AUTHENTICATION PIPELINES
Standard DB authentication: captures email/password → CustomUserDetailsService retrieves the user entity → BCryptPasswordEncoder validates credentials against the hashed database value.
Federated OAuth2: redirect to Google or GitHub → callback processed by OAuthAuthenticationSuccessHandler → extracts identity attributes (email, display name, avatar URL) → provisions a new account or syncs existing data.
GLOBAL CONTEXT PIPELINE — RootController.java
Configured via @ControllerAdvice to run across every controller endpoint. Reads the active Authentication token, queries UserService, and injects loggedInUser directly into the Spring Model.
Service & business logic
Data sanitization & DTO transfer — dedicated transfer models (ContactForm, ContactSearchForm) prevent over-posting vulnerabilities and decouple web requests from persistent entity schemas.
Media handling (ImageServiceImpl) — accepts MultipartFile input, generates a UUID-based public ID, uploads binary streams to Cloudinary over HTTPS, and retrieves the hosted CDN image URL.
Pagination & sorting — packages query parameters into PageRequest.of(page, size, Sort.by(direction, sortBy)) to enforce LIMIT/OFFSET execution at the database tier.
Data persistence — JPA & Hibernate
Entity relationships:
1. User → Contact: bidirectional one-to-many (@OneToMany(mappedBy = "user") / @ManyToOne)
1. Contact → SocialLink: bidirectional one-to-many (cascade = CascadeType.ALL, orphanRemoval = true)
Recursion guard — @ToString.Exclude and @EqualsAndHashCode.Exclude applied to circular navigation paths (Contact.user, User.contacts) to eliminate recursive logger crashes and memory overflows.

DocMind Information Security: Incident Response Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

1. Incident Classification
- Severity 1 (Critical): Active data exfiltration, total production downtime, or compromised root cryptographic keys. Response SLA: 15 minutes.
- Severity 2 (High): Partial service impairment, privilege escalation vulnerability, or credential leak on internal staging. Response SLA: 1 hour.
- Severity 3 (Low): Minor policy infractions, phishing attempts blocked by filters, or non-exploitable configuration warnings. Response SLA: 24 hours.

2. Containment Protocol
Upon detecting a Severity 1 breach, the Security Operations Center (SOC) lead has the authority to revoke active session JWT secrets, isolate impacted VPC subnets, and invoke disaster recovery failover.

3. Post-Incident Root Cause Analysis (RCA)
A blameless post-mortem document must be produced within 72 hours of incident closure, including timeline, contributing root causes, and corrective action items with designated owners.

DocMind Infrastructure & Microservices Architecture Specification

1. Service Decomposition
The platform is built on Spring Boot 3.3 microservices communicating via asynchronous event streams.
- Gateway Service: Spring Cloud Gateway routing incoming traffic, handling rate limiting at 500 requests per minute per API key.
- Document Ingestion Service: Handles file uploads, Tika/PDF text extraction, chunking, and vector embedding generation.
- Retrieval & Generation Service: Coordinates context retrieval from the vector store and orchestrates streaming responses via LLM providers.

2. Data Tier & Vector Indexing
- Primary Storage: MySQL 8.0 cluster hosting user profiles, document metadata, audit logs, and conversation threads.
- Vector Storage: Persistent vector embeddings indexed with cosine distance, operating at a minimum similarity threshold of 0.72 for production queries.

3. Monitoring and SLOs
The system targets 99.9% uptime. Prometheus scrapes service metrics every 15 seconds, and Grafana dashboards alert on P99 latency exceeding 2,500ms.

1.    CSCF             (Call         Session                 Control               Function)                                                                                                        

                  Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                             

                  The  CSCF    controls   SIP  signaling  in the  IMS   network.   It  manages   user  registration,                                                                                                  
                  authentication,   routing,  and  call/session   control.                                                                                                                                            

                  There  are  three  types   of CSCFs.                                                                                                                                                                

                  P-CSCF          (Proxy-CSCF)                                                                                                                                                                        

                  Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                             

                      ●    First IMS  node   contacted    by the  UE.                                                                                                                                                 
                      ●    Acts  as the  SIP  proxy.                                                                                                                                                                  
                      ●    Forwards    SIP  messages.                                                                                                                                                                 
                      ●    Maintains   a secure   connection    with  the  UE.                                                                                                                                        

                  Example                                                                                                                                                                                             

                  UE                                                                                                                                                                                                  
                   |                                                                                                                                                                                                  
                  REGISTER                                                                                                                                                                                            
                   |                                                                                                                                                                                                  
                  P-CSCF                                                                                                                                                                                              

                  I-CSCF         (Interrogating-CSCF)                                                                                                                                                                 

                  Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                             

                      ●    Entry  point of the  IMS   network.                                                                                                                                                        
                      ●    Queries   the HSS    to determine    which   S-CSCF     should   serve  the  subscriber.                                                                                                   
                      ●    Hides  the  internal  IMS  topology.                                                                                                                                                       

                  Uses:                                                                                                                                                                                               

                      ●    UAR/UAA                                                                                                                                                                                    
                      ●    LIR/LIA

Purpose

                      ●    Traffic control                                                                                                                                                                            
                      ●    Service  authorization                                                                                                                                                                     

                  PCRF    does   not  forward    user  traffic.                                                                                                                                                       

                  It  only  makes policy  decisions.

                  Subscriber   starts  YouTube.                                                                                                                                                                       

                  PCRF    decides                                                                                                                                                                                     

                  Maximum     bandwidth    =  20  Mbps                                                                                                                                                                

                  QoS   Class  =  Video                                                                                                                                                                               

                  Charging   Rule   = Premium                                                                                                                                                                         

                  Then   sends   these  rules  to the enforcement      function.

                   Interface               Peer                                                                                                                                                                       

                   Gx            PCEF                                                                                                                                                                                 

                   Sd            TDF                                                                                                                                                                                  

                   Rx            Application   Function

                  Based   on  the MVC    (Model-View-Controller)         pattern.                                                                                                                               

                                             Component                          Role                                                                                                                            

                                             Model             Holds   data  and  business    logic                                                                                                             

                                             View              Renders    UI  (JSP,  Thymeleaf)

                                    Client request                                                                                                                                                              
                                          ↓                                                                                                                                                                     
                                    DispatcherServlet          (Front  Controller  —   receives   all  requests)                                                                                                
                                          ↓                                                                                                                                                                     
                                    HandlerMapping             (finds correct  @Controller     method)                                                                                                          
                                          ↓                                                                                                                                                                     
                                    Controller                 (processes    request,  calls  Service)                                                                                                          
                                          ↓

                    Application    objects,  which    are  known    as Beans.                                                                                                                                   

                    Types    of Spring    Containers                                                                                                                                                            

                    Spring   provides    two  primary   container    interfaces   with  different  levels  of functionality:                                                                                    

                    01.  BeanFactory:                                                                                                                                                                           

                    The   simplest   and   most   lightweight   container.   It provides   basic   DI features    and  uses                                                                                     
                    lazy  initialization (beans    are  created   only  when    requested).                                                                                                                     

                    02.  ApplicationContext:                                                                                                                                                                    

                    An  advanced,     feature-rich    sub-interface    of BeanFactory.      It  is  the  standard choice   for                                                                                  
                    most   applications    because     it  adds enterprise-specific     features   like:                                                                                                        

                        ●    Internationalization    (i18n)   support.                                                                                                                                          
                        ●    Event   propagation     and  application    event   listeners.                                                                                                                     
                        ●    Easier  integration    with  Aspect-Oriented      Programming       (AOP).                                                                                                         
                        ●    Eager   initialization  by default   (beans   are  created    during   container   startup).                                                                                       

                    How    it  work                                                                                                                                                                             
                        ●    Reads   configuration   (XML,  Java   config, or annotations)                                                                                                                      
                        ●    Creates  objects   (beans)                                                                                                                                                         
                        ●    Manages    their lifecycle                                                                                                                                                         

              1    Metadata    Input               Developers    provide  "recipes"  (configuration)   for  beans.                                                                                              

              2    Container    Initialization     When   the  application  starts, an implementation     like                                                                                                  
                                                   AnnotationConfigApplicationContext        is created.                                                                                                        

              3    Bean   Assembly                 The  container  reads   the metadata,    finds the classes,  creates   instances,                                                                            
                                                   and  wires  them  together   according   to their  defined dependencies.                                                                                     

              4    Production                      The  result is a fully  configured system   where   objects  are  ready  to be                                                                               
                                                   used  by  the application.                                                                                                                                   

                    �   Example:                                                                                                                                                                                

                             ApplicationContext      context   =  new                                                                                                                                           
                             AnnotationConfigApplicationContext(AppConfig.class);
